key_insight: Neural limit order book generators trained only for next-token prediction exhibit emergent market impact, although the observed scaling differs from the traditional square-root law.
engineering_relevance: This financial-market simulation benchmark—not a materials-discovery study—tests whether generative models provide realistic trading environments for agent training.
method: Measure order-flow persistence and price diffusivity during free generation.
Inject execution-style metaorders and compare visible injections with blind simulator-only controls to isolate learned responses.
Estimate impact scaling and amplitude, then measure post-execution relaxation.
evidence_signal: Evaluation of five autoregressive models across five NASDAQ stocks found impact exponents of 0.63–1.21, versus the traditional 0.5, with estimators validated on baselines with known dynamics.
watch_item: No post-execution impact decay was observed in the tested models; short context windows are a tentative explanation, not an established cause.
paper_title: LOB-Impact Benchmark: Emergent Market Impact in Generative Limit Order Book Models
